text:
alex: FYI we just had a nasty interaction during the preemptible GPU scale-down in us-west. cluster-autoscaler started removing nodes but several pods were stuck because of PodDisruptionBudgets. CA gave up and we ended up with stranded surfacing failures :warning:

infra-bot: alert: CA-scale-down-failed (nodepool=preemptible-gpu-us-west) - 12 nodes queued, 5 blocked by PDBs

maria: ugh. which PDBs ended up blocking? any long-running jobs or statefulsets?

alex: mostly model-training jobs and a couple of sidecars that set cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=false. PDBs had minAvailable: 1 so eviction would violate them. snippet from kubelet logs:
```
I0325 03:12:08.123 12345 eviction_manager.go:971] eviction failed: PodDisruptionBudget violation for pod model-train-xyz
```

ryan: CA is doing the right thing — it won't evict if PDB prevents it. We need a pattern: make low-priority GPU workloads explicitly evictable and avoid PDBs that block scale-down.

maria: agree. propose checklist for preemptible nodepools: 1) mark non-critical pods with a low PriorityClass; 2) ensure safe-to-evict annotation exists or remove PDBs that are unnecessary; 3) enable a 'drain leash' automation to force-evict after human approval window.

ryan: +1. concrete examples: create a low-priority class for preemptible workloads:
```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: preemptible-gpu-low
value: 100
globalDefault: false
description: Low priority for interruptible GPU jobs
```
And for pods that should be evictable make sure they do NOT set cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: 'false' (or set it to 'true').

alex: on PDBs we should prefer maxUnavailable where possible. current problematic PDBs use minAvailable: 1 on small ReplicaSets which blocks node removal. change example PDB to allow one pod to go down:
```yaml
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: model-train-pdb
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: model-train
```

maria: another operational knob: annotate pods that truly must not be evicted with cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: 'false' and keep that list tiny (ingress controllers, metrics exporters etc). everything else should be evictable.

ryan: also consider adjusting CA flags for the preemptible pool: lower scale-down-unneeded-time and set max-empty-bulk-delete to avoid long waits. but that doesn't fix PDBs.

sre-oncall: we hit a second-order problem where CA tried to remove many nodes simultaneously and our scheduler couldn't reschedule because of region constraints. suggestion: limit CA max-empty-bulk-delete to 2 for GPU pools and enable a cooldown between deletes.

alex: ops automation proposal — add a small controller (drain-leash) that: 1) detects a drain that stalls due to PDB violation for > 10m, 2) posts a slack approval webhook, 3) if approved, runs a safe sequence: cordon -> copy critical pods to another pool if possible -> evict lower-priority pods -> uncordon leftovers. fallback option: force-drain after manual sign-off.

maria: sounds good. rough drain sequence we should document in runbook: 
- cordon node
- try graceful drain: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=5m
- if drain fails due to PDB, check PDB violation report: kubectl get pdb -o wide
- if violation is caused by low-priority workload, patch deployment to reduce replicas or temporarily set maxUnavailable, or scale-up burst capacity to absorb pods
- last resort: force-evict with eviction API and annotate incident

ryan: command references:
```bash
# show blocking pdbs for a node
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=NODE_NAME
# simulate eviction check
kubectl drain NODE_NAME --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --dry-run=client
```

alex: Action items: maria to draft the drain-leash controller design + slack approval flow, ryan to inventory current PDBs and mark candidates for conversion to maxUnavailable, i'll tweak CA flags for preemptible GPU pools and limit bulk deletes.

maria: I'll start a PR with runbook snippets and the PriorityClass YAML. tagging @ryan for PDB list. :thumbsup:

ryan: will run an audit and send a short list by EOD. also will add a small k8s job that alerts if any PDB minAvailable > 0 for ReplicaSets with replicas <=2 — those are dangerous for scale-down.

sre-oncall: creating an on-call playbook entry now. if we see another incident, use the 'force-evict after approval' checklist.

alex: thanks. can we add an automated smoke test for scale-down in staging? simulate CA removing a node and assert no PodDisruptionBudget blocks finalization. if that passes we can roll to prod. :eyes:
